questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, and its SI unit is the pascal (1 Pa = 1 N m⁻²).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of work (or energy)?
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance = MLT⁻² × L = ML²T⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many significant figures are there in the measurement 6.020 × 10³ kg?
questions.explanation: The digits 6, 0, 2 and the trailing 0 after the decimal point are all significant, giving 4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The radius of a sphere is measured with a possible error of 2%. What is the possible percentage error in its calculated volume?
questions.explanation: Volume ∝ r³, so the fractional error in V is 3 × 2% = 6%.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: From Newton's law of gravitation F = G m₁m₂ / r², what is the dimensional formula of the gravitational constant G?
questions.explanation: G = F r² / (m₁m₂) = (MLT⁻²)(L²)/M² = M⁻¹L³T⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which pair of physical quantities has the same dimensions?
questions.explanation: Torque (force × distance) and energy both have dimensions ML²T⁻²; the other pairs differ.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is a light year? Is it a unit of time or of distance?
questions.answer: A light year is a unit of distance: the distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year, about 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m.
keyPoints: It is a unit of distance, not time
Distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year
questions.explanation: Light travels about 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, so in one year it covers roughly 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A resistance is found from R = V/I, with V = (100 ± 5) V and I = (10 ± 0.2) A. Find the maximum percentage error in R.
keyPoints: For a quotient, add percentage errors: 5% + 2% = 7%
questions.explanation: In a quotient the maximum fractional errors add, so ΔR/R = 5% + 2% = 7%.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In a position–time graph, what does the slope of the graph give?
questions.explanation: Slope of x–t graph = dx/dt, which is velocity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The area under a velocity–time graph between two instants gives
questions.explanation: Area under a v–t graph is the integral of v dt, which is displacement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s⁻² for 5 s. What distance does it cover in this time?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and ignoring air resistance, what maximum height does it reach?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A body falls freely from rest. What is the ratio of the distances covered in the 1st, 2nd and 3rd seconds?
questions.explanation: Distance in the nth second = ½g(2n−1), so the distances are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A stone dropped from the top of a tower reaches the ground after 4 s. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what distance does it cover in the last second of its fall?
questions.explanation: Height in 4 s = ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 m; in 3 s = 45 m; last second = 80 − 45 = 35 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A car travelling at 72 km/h is brought to rest by uniform braking in 5 s. Find the deceleration and the stopping distance.
questions.answer: Deceleration = 4 m s⁻²; stopping distance = 50 m.
questions.explanation: Convert 72 km/h to 20 m s⁻¹, then use v = u + at and s = average speed × time.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 30 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find the time of flight until it returns to the thrower's hand and the maximum height reached.
questions.answer: Time of flight = 6 s; maximum height = 45 m.
questions.explanation: The motion up and down is symmetric, so the total time is twice u/g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; the others are scalars.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: For a given speed of projection (no air resistance, level ground), the horizontal range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is
questions.explanation: Range = u² sin 2θ / g is maximum when sin 2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the magnitude of the resultant of two perpendicular forces of 3 N and 4 N?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its time of flight on level ground?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A projectile fired at 15° to the horizontal has the same horizontal range as another projectile fired with the same speed at which angle?
questions.explanation: Range depends on sin 2θ, which is equal for complementary angles θ and 90° − θ; the complement of 15° is 75°.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a horizontal circle at constant speed. If the string suddenly breaks, in what direction does the stone initially move (ignoring gravity for the moment of release)?
options: Along the tangent to the circle at that point
questions.explanation: With no net force, the stone continues with its instantaneous velocity, which is tangent to the circle.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A body moves in a circle of radius 0.5 m with a constant speed of 5 m s⁻¹. Find its centripetal acceleration.
questions.answer: 50 m s⁻² directed towards the centre.
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is v²/r = 25/0.5 = 50 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown horizontally at 15 m s⁻¹ from the top of an 80 m high cliff. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the time taken to reach the ground and the horizontal distance covered.
keyPoints: Vertical motion: 80 = ½ × 10 × t², so t = 4 s
questions.explanation: Vertical and horizontal motions are independent; the fall time fixes the horizontal distance.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which physical quantity is a measure of the inertia of a body?
questions.explanation: The greater the mass, the greater the inertia (resistance to change in the state of motion).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Newton's first law of motion gives the concept of
questions.explanation: The first law states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted on by an external force; this property is inertia.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A net force of 20 N acts on a 5 kg block. What is the acceleration of the block?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 10 kg block rests on a horizontal surface with coefficient of static friction 0.4. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the maximum static friction force?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 60 kg person stands on a weighing scale in a lift that accelerates upward at 2 m s⁻². Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what does the scale read (as a force)?
questions.explanation: N − mg = ma, so N = m(g + a) = 60 × 12 = 720 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Blocks of 2 kg and 3 kg touch each other on a smooth horizontal table. A horizontal force of 10 N pushes the 2 kg block towards the 3 kg block. What force does the 2 kg block exert on the 3 kg block?
questions.explanation: Common acceleration = 10/5 = 2 m s⁻²; the force on the 3 kg block is 3 × 2 = 6 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A bullet of mass 20 g is fired at 300 m s⁻¹ from a gun of mass 4 kg. Find the recoil speed of the gun.
keyPoints: Total momentum before firing is zero
V = 6/4 = 1.5 m s⁻¹, opposite to the bullet
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum gives the gun a momentum equal and opposite to the bullet's (6 kg m s⁻¹).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A block just begins to slide on a rough plane when the plane is tilted to 30° with the horizontal. Find the coefficient of static friction.
keyPoints: At the point of sliding, mg sinθ = μ mg cosθ
questions.explanation: At the angle of repose the component of weight along the plane equals the limiting friction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 watt = 1 J s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In uniform circular motion, the work done by the centripetal force is
questions.explanation: The force is perpendicular to the displacement at every instant, so W = Fs cos 90° = 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving at 3 m s⁻¹?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A force of 10 N moves a body through 5 m. The force makes an angle of 60° with the displacement. How much work does the force do?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The momentum of a body is increased by 100%. By what percentage does its kinetic energy increase?
questions.explanation: KE = p²/2m. Doubling p makes KE four times, an increase of 300%.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A pump raises 100 kg of water through a height of 20 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the power delivered to the water?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A spring of force constant 200 N m⁻¹ is compressed by 0.1 m. Find the elastic potential energy stored.
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy of a spring is ½kx² = 0.5 × 200 × 0.01 = 1 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is dropped from a height of 10 m. Using energy conservation and g = 10 m s⁻², find its speed just before it hits the ground (ignore air resistance).
keyPoints: Loss of PE = gain of KE: mgh = ½mv²
v ≈ 14.1 m s⁻¹, independent of mass
questions.explanation: Equating mgh to ½mv² gives v = √200 ≈ 14.1 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of torque?
questions.explanation: Torque = force × perpendicular distance, with unit newton metre.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a rigid body depends on
options: its mass distribution and the position of the axis
questions.explanation: I = Σmr² depends on how the mass is distributed about the chosen axis.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the moment of inertia of a thin ring of mass M and radius R about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its plane?
questions.explanation: All the mass is at distance R from the axis, so I = MR².

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A force of 10 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.3 m from an axis. What is the torque about the axis?

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A spinning skater pulls her arms in. Her angular momentum is conserved. What happens to her rotational kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: KE = L²/2I; I decreases while L is fixed, so KE increases (she does internal work pulling the arms in).

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A solid disc and a ring of the same mass and radius roll without slipping from rest down the same incline. Which reaches the bottom first?
questions.explanation: The disc has a smaller moment of inertia, so less energy goes into rotation and it has a larger acceleration (g sinθ / (1 + k²/R²)).

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A wheel of moment of inertia 0.5 kg m² rotates at 20 rad s⁻¹. Find its angular momentum and rotational kinetic energy.
questions.answer: L = 10 kg m² s⁻¹; KE = 100 J.
questions.explanation: Use L = Iω and KE = ½Iω².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which scientist gave the three laws of planetary motion?
questions.explanation: Johannes Kepler formulated the three laws of planetary motion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Kepler's second law (equal areas swept in equal times) is a consequence of conservation of
questions.explanation: The gravitational force is central, so torque about the Sun is zero and angular momentum is conserved.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: At a height equal to the radius of the Earth above its surface, the acceleration due to gravity is
questions.explanation: g' = g R²/(R + h)² = g R²/(2R)² = g/4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The escape speed from the Earth's surface compared with the orbital speed of a satellite just above the surface is
questions.explanation: v_e = √(2gR) and v_o = √(gR), so v_e = √2 v_o (about 11.2 km s⁻¹ versus 7.9 km s⁻¹).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Assuming the Earth to be a uniform sphere, what is the weight of a body of mass m at the centre of the Earth?
questions.explanation: Inside a uniform sphere g falls linearly with distance from the centre and is zero at the centre.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A satellite is moved from an orbit of radius r to one of radius 4r around the same planet. By what factor does its time period change?
questions.explanation: By Kepler's third law T² ∝ r³, so T ∝ r^{3/2} = 4^{3/2} = 8 times.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A planet has twice the mass and twice the radius of the Earth. Find its surface gravity in terms of the Earth's g.
questions.explanation: Doubling mass doubles g, doubling radius divides g by 4, so the net factor is 1/2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Stress is defined as
questions.explanation: Stress is the internal restoring force per unit cross-sectional area.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of Young's modulus?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus = stress/strain, and strain is dimensionless, so it has the unit of stress, N m⁻² or pascal.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire of original length 2 m stretches by 1 mm under a load. What is the longitudinal strain?
questions.explanation: Strain = ΔL/L = 1 × 10⁻³ m / 2 m = 5 × 10⁻⁴.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire of cross-section 1 mm² and Young's modulus 2 × 10¹¹ Pa carries a tensile force of 100 N. What is the strain produced?
questions.explanation: Stress = 100 / 10⁻⁶ = 10⁸ Pa, so strain = 10⁸ / (2 × 10¹¹) = 5 × 10⁻⁴.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two wires of the same material and length have radii r and 2r. The same load is hung from each. What is the ratio of the extension of the thinner wire to that of the thicker wire?
questions.explanation: Extension = FL/(πr²Y) ∝ 1/r², so the ratio is (1/r²) : (1/4r²) = 4 : 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume in a stretched wire is
questions.explanation: Energy = ½ × F × ΔL, and dividing by volume AL gives ½ × (F/A) × (ΔL/L).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A steel wire of length 3 m and cross-section 2 × 10⁻⁶ m² carries a load of 40 N. Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻². Find the extension.
questions.explanation: Substituting in Y = FL/(AΔL) gives ΔL = 3 × 10⁻⁴ m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A hydraulic lift works on the principle of
questions.explanation: Pascal's law says pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of the coefficient of viscosity?
questions.explanation: η = F/(A · dv/dx) has unit N s m⁻² = Pa s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and density of water 1000 kg m⁻³, what is the gauge pressure at a depth of 10 m in water?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In a hydraulic lift the large piston has 50 times the area of the small piston. A force of 100 N is applied to the small piston. What force acts on the large piston?
questions.explanation: Pressure is the same, so F₂ = F₁ × (A₂/A₁) = 100 × 50 = 5000 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A block of density 600 kg m⁻³ floats in water of density 1000 kg m⁻³. What fraction of its volume is submerged?
questions.explanation: For floating, weight = buoyant force: ρ_block V = ρ_water V_sub, so V_sub/V = 0.6.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Water flows steadily through a horizontal pipe whose radius is reduced to half. How does the flow speed in the narrow part compare with that in the wide part?
questions.explanation: Equation of continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂. Area becomes one-quarter, so the speed becomes 4 times.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Find the excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius 2 cm if the surface tension of the soap solution is 0.03 N m⁻¹.
keyPoints: A soap bubble has two surfaces, so ΔP = 4S/r
questions.explanation: Two liquid surfaces each contribute 2S/r, giving ΔP = 4S/r = 6 Pa.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Water (surface tension 0.07 N m⁻¹, density 1000 kg m⁻³, contact angle 0°) rises in a capillary tube of radius 0.5 mm. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the height of the rise.
questions.explanation: Capillary rise follows h = 2S cosθ/(rρg), giving 0.028 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Absolute zero on the Celsius scale is approximately
questions.explanation: Absolute zero (0 K) corresponds to −273.15 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: While ice melts at 0 °C, the heat supplied
options: is lost to the surroundings only
changes its state without changing its temperature
questions.explanation: The heat supplied is latent heat; it breaks the structure of the solid while the temperature stays constant.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 10 °C? (Specific heat of water = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.)

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 100 m long steel rail has α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. By how much does it expand when its temperature rises by 50 °C?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: 100 g of water at 80 °C is mixed with 100 g of water at 20 °C in an insulated container. What is the final temperature?
questions.explanation: With equal masses and the same specific heat, the final temperature is the average, 50 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to Stefan–Boltzmann law, the power radiated by a black body is proportional to T⁴. If its absolute temperature is doubled, the power radiated becomes
questions.explanation: Power ∝ T⁴, so doubling T multiplies the power by 2⁴ = 16.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How much heat is needed to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 °C? The latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Heat needed for a change of state is mL = 0.5 × 3.36 × 10⁵ J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of conservation of
questions.explanation: It states that heat supplied to a system equals the increase in internal energy plus the work done by the system.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in internal energy is
questions.explanation: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, which stays constant.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. What is the change in its internal energy?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the efficiency of a Carnot engine working between 600 K and 300 K?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A gas at a constant pressure of 2 × 10⁵ Pa expands from 1 litre to 3 litres (1 litre = 10⁻³ m³). How much work does it do?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: An ideal gas is compressed adiabatically. What happens to its temperature?
questions.explanation: With Q = 0, the work done on the gas increases its internal energy, so its temperature rises.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A Carnot engine has a source at 400 K and a sink at 300 K. Find its efficiency and the work done per cycle if it absorbs 1000 J from the source.
questions.explanation: Work output is the efficiency times the heat absorbed from the source.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The number of molecules in one mole of a substance is
questions.explanation: This is Avogadro's number, 6.022 × 10²³ per mole.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is directly proportional to its
questions.explanation: Average KE per molecule = (3/2)k_B T.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many degrees of freedom does a monatomic gas molecule have?
questions.explanation: A monatomic molecule has three translational degrees of freedom.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: If the absolute temperature of a gas is made four times, its rms speed becomes
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ √T, so quadrupling T doubles v_rms.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: At the same temperature, what is the ratio of the rms speed of hydrogen (molar mass 2 g/mol) to that of oxygen (molar mass 32 g/mol)?
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ 1/√M, so the ratio is √(32/2) = √16 = 4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: 2 mol of an ideal gas occupy 5 litres at 300 K. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what is the approximate pressure?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Find the total translational kinetic energy of 1 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K. (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Translational KE of one mole is (3/2)RT = 3739.5 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration of the particle is directly proportional to its
questions.explanation: The defining condition of SHM is a = −ω²x.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The frequency f and time period T of an oscillation are related by
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second, f = 1/T.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the time period of a simple pendulum of length 1 m? (Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².)

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 0.5 kg mass is attached to a spring of force constant 200 N m⁻¹. What is the time period of its oscillations?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 0.1 m and frequency 5 Hz. What is its maximum speed?
questions.explanation: ω = 2πf = 10π rad s⁻¹; v_max = Aω = 0.1 × 31.4 = 3.14 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The length of a simple pendulum is made four times. Its time period
questions.explanation: T ∝ √l, so four times the length gives twice the time period.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 0.2 kg particle performs SHM with angular frequency 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.05 m. Find its total mechanical energy.
questions.explanation: Total energy in SHM is ½mω²A² = 0.025 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Sound waves in air are
questions.explanation: Air particles vibrate along the direction of propagation, forming compressions and rarefactions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The speed v, frequency f and wavelength λ of a wave are related by
questions.explanation: A wave travels one wavelength in each period, so v = λ/T = fλ.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A sound wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.68 m. What is its speed?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A string of length L fixed at both ends has a wave speed v. What is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: In the fundamental mode L = λ/2, so f = v/λ = v/2L.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A pipe closed at one end is 0.85 m long. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, what is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe f = v/4L = 340/(4 × 0.85) = 100 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. What is the beat frequency?
questions.explanation: Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂| = 4 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A travelling wave is described by y = 0.02 sin(10πt − πx) in SI units. Find its amplitude, frequency, wavelength and speed.
questions.answer: Amplitude 0.02 m; frequency 5 Hz; wavelength 2 m; speed 10 m s⁻¹.
keyPoints: Compare with y = A sin(ωt − kx): A = 0.02 m
ω = 10π gives f = ω/2π = 5 Hz; k = π gives λ = 2π/k = 2 m
questions.explanation: Reading A, ω and k from the equation gives f, λ and v = ω/k = 10 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an SI base unit?
questions.explanation: The newton is a derived unit (kg m s⁻²); kelvin, ampere and mole are base units.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The SI prefix 'micro' stands for a factor of
questions.explanation: Micro means one millionth, 10⁻⁶.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = MLT⁻² / L² = ML⁻¹T⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In a vernier callipers, 10 vernier divisions coincide with 9 main-scale divisions, and one main-scale division is 1 mm. What is the least count?
questions.explanation: Least count = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = 1 mm − 0.9 mm = 0.1 mm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which expression for the time period of a mass m attached to a spring of force constant k is dimensionally consistent?
questions.explanation: k has dimensions MT⁻², so m/k has dimensions T² and √(m/k) has dimensions of time.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: g is found from g = 4π²L/T². The length L is measured with 1% error and the time period T with 2% error. What is the maximum percentage error in g?
questions.explanation: Fractional error = ΔL/L + 2ΔT/T = 1% + 4% = 5%.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Convert a density of 1 g cm⁻³ into kg m⁻³.
questions.explanation: Dividing 10⁻³ kg by 10⁻⁶ m³ gives 1000 kg m⁻³.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Using dimensional analysis, show that the time period T of a simple pendulum depends on its length l and the acceleration due to gravity g as T ∝ √(l/g). Assume T depends only on l, g and mass m.
questions.answer: Writing T ∝ m^a l^b g^c and equating dimensions gives a = 0, b = ½, c = −½, so T ∝ √(l/g).
keyPoints: Write T = k m^a l^b g^c
Equate dimensions: M: a = 0; L: b + c = 0; T: −2c = 1
So c = −½, b = ½, a = 0, hence T ∝ √(l/g)
questions.explanation: Matching powers of M, L and T on both sides fixes the exponents; the mass drops out.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The rate of change of velocity of a body with time is called
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = dv/dt.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A body moving with uniform velocity has an acceleration that is
questions.explanation: Uniform velocity means velocity does not change, so acceleration is zero.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle with initial speed 10 m s⁻¹ moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s⁻² over a distance of 24 m. What is its final speed?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A car travels the first half of a journey at 40 km/h and the second half (same distance) at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed = 2v₁v₂/(v₁ + v₂) = 2 × 40 × 60/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Car A moves at a constant 20 m s⁻¹. Car B starts from rest at the same place and the same instant with a constant acceleration of 2 m s⁻² in the same direction. After how long does B overtake A?
questions.explanation: They meet when 20t = ½ × 2 × t², so t = 20 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball thrown vertically upward reaches its highest point. At that instant its acceleration is
questions.explanation: Only the velocity is zero at the top; gravity continues to act, so the acceleration is g directed downward.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The position of a particle is x = 3t² + 2t (x in metres, t in seconds). Find its velocity at t = 2 s and its acceleration.
questions.answer: Velocity at t = 2 s is 14 m s⁻¹; acceleration is 6 m s⁻² (constant).
keyPoints: At t = 2 s, v = 14 m s⁻¹
questions.explanation: Differentiate the position once for velocity and twice for acceleration.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward at 20 m s⁻¹ from the top of a 25 m high building (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find the time it takes to reach the ground and its speed on arrival.
questions.answer: Time = 5 s; speed on arrival = 30 m s⁻¹.
keyPoints: v = 20 − 10 × 5 = −30, so speed 30 m s⁻¹ downward
questions.explanation: Solving the displacement equation with the final position 25 m below the start gives t = 5 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the magnitude of a unit vector?
questions.explanation: A unit vector has magnitude one and only specifies a direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In uniform circular motion, which of the following remains constant?
questions.explanation: The speed is constant, but the direction of velocity (and hence velocity, momentum and acceleration as vectors) keeps changing.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: For vectors A = 2î + 3ĵ and B = 4î − ĵ, what is the scalar product A · B?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what maximum height does it reach?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: If the launch speed of a projectile is doubled while the angle of projection is kept the same, its horizontal range becomes
questions.explanation: Range R = u² sin 2θ / g is proportional to u², so doubling u gives 4 times the range.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A boat can move at 5 m s⁻¹ in still water. It is steered perpendicular to the bank of a river flowing at 3 m s⁻¹. What is the boat's speed relative to the ground?
questions.explanation: The two velocities are perpendicular, so v = √(5² + 3²) = √34 ≈ 5.8 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Resolve a force of 50 N acting at 30° above the horizontal into horizontal and vertical components.
questions.explanation: The components are F cosθ along the horizontal and F sinθ along the vertical.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A cyclist rides at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹ around a circular track of radius 20 m. Find the centripetal acceleration, the angular speed and the time for one lap.
questions.answer: a = 5 m s⁻²; ω = 0.5 rad s⁻¹; time for one lap = 4π s ≈ 12.6 s.
questions.explanation: Use a = v²/r, ω = v/r and T = 2π/ω.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of linear momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity, so its unit is kg m s⁻¹ (equivalent to N s).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to Newton's third law, the action and reaction forces
options: cancel each other on the same body
questions.explanation: They are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction and act on two different bodies, so they cannot cancel each other.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A force of 50 N acts on a body for 0.2 s. What is the impulse?
questions.explanation: Impulse = F Δt = 50 × 0.2 = 10 N s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 0.15 kg ball moving at 20 m s⁻¹ is stopped by a player's hand in 0.1 s. What average force does the hand exert?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two masses of 3 kg and 5 kg hang from the ends of a light string passing over a smooth light pulley (an Atwood machine). Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the acceleration of the masses?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 10 kg block on a rough horizontal floor is pulled by a horizontal force of 30 N. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2 and g = 10 m s⁻². What is the acceleration of the block?
questions.explanation: Friction = 0.2 × 100 = 20 N; net force = 10 N; a = 10/10 = 1 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A car of mass 1500 kg must accelerate at 2 m s⁻² against a constant resistive force of 500 N. What forward force must the engine supply through the wheels?
questions.explanation: The driving force must provide the net force and also overcome the resistance.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A car rounds a flat circular bend of radius 50 m. The coefficient of friction between the tyres and road is 0.5. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the maximum speed with which the car can turn without skidding.
questions.answer: About 15.8 m s⁻¹ (√250 m s⁻¹, about 57 km/h).
keyPoints: Friction provides the centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r
questions.explanation: The maximum friction μmg supplies the centripetal force mv²/r, independent of the car's mass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to the work–energy theorem, the net work done on a body equals the change in its
questions.explanation: W_net = ΔKE.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a conservative force?
questions.explanation: Work done by gravity depends only on the end points, not on the path, so it is conservative.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the gravitational potential energy of a 5 kg body raised to a height of 4 m? (Take g = 10 m s⁻².)

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A machine of power 500 W works for 2 minutes. How much work does it do?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball collides head-on elastically with an identical stationary ball. What happens after the collision?
options: The first ball stops and the second moves off with the first one's speed
Both move with half the original speed
The first ball rebounds with the original speed
questions.explanation: For an elastic head-on collision between equal masses, the velocities are exchanged.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 2 kg body moving at 6 m s⁻¹ collides with a 4 kg body at rest and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost?
questions.explanation: Common speed = 12/6 = 2 m s⁻¹; KE falls from ½ × 2 × 36 = 36 J to ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 J, a loss of 24 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How much work does gravity do on a 2 kg ball that falls through 5 m? (g = 10 m s⁻².)
keyPoints: = 100 J (positive, since the force and displacement are in the same direction)
questions.explanation: The work done by gravity is mgh, equal to the gain in kinetic energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 2 kg block slides from rest down a smooth incline from a vertical height of 1.8 m (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find its speed at the bottom.
keyPoints: The incline is smooth, so mechanical energy is conserved
questions.explanation: The speed depends only on the vertical drop, not on the angle or the mass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Where is the centre of mass of a uniform thin rod?
options: One-third of the length from one end
One-quarter of the length from one end
questions.explanation: By symmetry, the centre of mass of a uniform rod is at its midpoint.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the SI unit of angular momentum?
questions.explanation: L = Iω has unit kg m² s⁻¹ (equivalently J s).

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A 1 kg mass is at x = 0 and a 3 kg mass is at x = 4 m on a line. Where is their centre of mass?

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A torque of 20 N m acts on a wheel of moment of inertia 5 kg m². What is its angular acceleration?
questions.explanation: α = τ/I = 20/5 = 4 rad s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a uniform rod of mass M and length L about a perpendicular axis through its centre is ML²/12. What is it about a parallel axis through one end?
questions.explanation: Parallel axis theorem: I = ML²/12 + M(L/2)² = ML²/3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A solid sphere rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface. What fraction of its total kinetic energy is rotational?
questions.explanation: Rotational KE = ½ × (2/5)mv² = mv²/5; total = 7mv²/10; the fraction is 2/7.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Why is it easier to push open a door by applying the force at the edge farthest from the hinges than near the hinges?
questions.answer: The torque is force × perpendicular distance from the hinge; a larger distance gives a larger torque for the same force.
keyPoints: Turning effect is torque τ = r F sinθ
Distance from the hinge (axis) is larger at the edge
So the same force gives a larger torque there
questions.explanation: A bigger lever arm means a smaller force is needed to produce the required torque.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The gravitational force between two masses is
options: attractive or repulsive depending on the masses
questions.explanation: Gravitation between any two masses is always attractive.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of the universal gravitational constant G?
questions.explanation: From F = Gm₁m₂/r², G = F r²/(m₁m₂), so its unit is N m² kg⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², what is the gravitational force between two 1 kg masses 1 m apart?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and the radius of the Earth as 6400 km, what is the orbital speed of a satellite revolving just above the Earth's surface?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What minimum work must be done to take a body of mass m from the Earth's surface to infinity (R = radius, g = surface gravity)?
questions.explanation: The surface potential energy is −GMm/R = −mgR, so mgR of work is required.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The total mechanical energy of a satellite in a circular orbit around a planet is
options: positive and equal to its kinetic energy
negative and twice its kinetic energy in magnitude
negative and equal in magnitude to its kinetic energy
questions.explanation: KE = GMm/2r and PE = −GMm/r, so total energy = −GMm/2r, equal in magnitude to the KE.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the acceleration due to gravity at a depth equal to half the Earth's radius below the surface, in terms of the surface value g?
keyPoints: g at depth d is g(1 − d/R)
questions.explanation: Inside a uniform Earth, g decreases linearly with depth.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to
questions.explanation: This is Hooke's law: stress ∝ strain.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which modulus of elasticity describes the change in volume of a body under uniform pressure?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus = pressure change / fractional change in volume.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A pressure increase of 10⁷ Pa decreases the volume of a liquid by 0.01% (a fractional change of 10⁻⁴). What is its bulk modulus?
questions.explanation: B = ΔP/(ΔV/V) = 10⁷/10⁻⁴ = 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of these materials has the largest Young's modulus?
questions.explanation: Steel has Young's modulus of about 2 × 10¹¹ Pa, much larger than lead, rubber or aluminium.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The extension of a wire under a load is doubled by increasing the load (within the elastic limit). How does the elastic potential energy stored in the wire change?
questions.explanation: Energy = ½ × (YA/L) × (ΔL)², which is proportional to the square of the extension, so it becomes 4 times.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire of length L stretches by x under a load F. A second wire of the same material and cross-section, with length L/2, carries the same load. What is its extension?
questions.explanation: Extension ΔL = FL/(AY) is proportional to the length, so the shorter wire stretches by x/2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Distinguish between elastic and plastic behaviour of a material.
questions.answer: A body is elastic if it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed; if the deformation remains after the force is removed (beyond the elastic limit), the behaviour is plastic.
keyPoints: Elastic: complete recovery when force is removed
The elastic limit separates the two
questions.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit a material no longer fully recovers its original dimensions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The upward buoyant force on a body immersed in a fluid equals the weight of the fluid displaced. This statement is known as
questions.explanation: This is Archimedes' principle.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of surface tension?
questions.explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length, so its unit is N m⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of 5 m in a liquid of density 800 kg m⁻³? (Take g = 10 m s⁻².)

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A body weighs 5 N in air and 3 N when fully immersed in water. What is the buoyant force on it?
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = apparent loss of weight = 5 − 3 = 2 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Water flows steadily in a horizontal pipe, at 2 m s⁻¹ in the wide part and 6 m s⁻¹ in the narrow part. By how much is the pressure in the wide part higher? (Density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³.)
questions.explanation: Bernoulli: ΔP = ½ρ(v₂² − v₁²) = ½ × 1000 × (36 − 4) = 16000 Pa.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The terminal velocity of a small sphere falling through a viscous liquid is proportional to the square of its radius. If the radius is doubled (same material), the terminal velocity becomes
questions.explanation: v_t ∝ r², so doubling r gives 4 times the terminal velocity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Water flows out through a small hole in the side of a tank, 5 m below the free surface. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the speed of efflux.
questions.explanation: Applying Bernoulli's principle between the surface and the hole gives v = √(2gh).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Explain, using Bernoulli's principle, why the roof of a house may be lifted off during a strong storm.
questions.answer: Fast-moving air over the roof has lower pressure than the still air inside the house, so a net upward force acts on the roof.
keyPoints: Air speed above the roof is high
By Bernoulli's principle, high speed means low pressure
Pressure difference between inside and outside gives a net upward force
questions.explanation: The pressure below the roof is greater than the pressure above it, producing upward lift.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following substances has the highest specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: Water has a very high specific heat, about 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth mainly by
questions.explanation: Radiation does not need a material medium, so it can travel through space.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A temperature of 300 K corresponds to what Celsius temperature (taking 0 °C = 273 K)?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: 0.2 kg of water cools from 100 °C to 50 °C. How much heat does it lose? (c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.)

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The ends of a metal rod 1 m long and 1 cm² in cross-section are held at 100 °C and 0 °C. Its thermal conductivity is 400 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the steady rate of heat flow along the rod?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: 100 g of ice at 0 °C is added to 400 g of water at 20 °C in an insulated container. (Latent heat of fusion of ice = 80 cal g⁻¹; specific heat of water = 1 cal g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.) What is the final state?
options: All the ice melts; mixture at 0 °C
All the ice melts; mixture at 10 °C
questions.explanation: Cooling the water to 0 °C releases 400 × 20 = 8000 cal, which exactly melts 100 g of ice (100 × 80 = 8000 cal).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon when both are at room temperature?
questions.answer: Metal is a better conductor of heat, so it draws heat from the hand faster than wood, which feels colder.
keyPoints: Both spoons are at the same temperature
Heat leaves the hand faster into the metal
questions.explanation: The sensation of cold depends on the rate of heat loss from the skin, not just on temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The zeroth law of thermodynamics leads to the concept of
questions.explanation: If two bodies are each in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other, which defines temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In which of the following processes is the work done by the gas zero?
questions.explanation: In an isochoric (constant-volume) process ΔV = 0, so W = PΔV = 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A refrigerator works between 270 K (inside) and 300 K (outside). What is its maximum coefficient of performance?
questions.explanation: COP = T_cold/(T_hot − T_cold) = 270/30 = 9.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A heat engine absorbs 800 J from the source and rejects 600 J to the sink in each cycle. What is its efficiency?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: One mole of an ideal gas at 300 K expands isothermally to double its volume. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ln 2 = 0.693, how much work does it do?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: For one mole of an ideal gas, the difference between the molar specific heats at constant pressure and constant volume, Cp − Cv, equals
questions.explanation: Mayer's relation: Cp − Cv = R.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: State the Kelvin–Planck statement of the second law of thermodynamics.
questions.answer: It is impossible to construct a heat engine that, working in a cycle, takes heat from a single reservoir and converts it entirely into work.
keyPoints: Heat engine operating in a cycle
Heat taken from a single reservoir
Cannot be completely converted into work (efficiency cannot be 100%)
questions.explanation: Some heat must always be rejected to a colder sink.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: At constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its
questions.explanation: This is Boyle's law: PV = constant at constant temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to Charles's law, at constant pressure the volume of a fixed mass of gas is
options: inversely proportional to its absolute temperature
proportional to the square of its temperature
directly proportional to its absolute temperature
questions.explanation: V/T = constant at constant pressure, with T in kelvin.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the approximate volume of one mole of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (0 °C, 1 atm)?
questions.explanation: The molar volume of an ideal gas at STP is 22.4 litres.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A gas has density 1.2 kg m⁻³ and rms molecular speed 500 m s⁻¹. Using P = ⅓ρv²_rms, what is its pressure?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to the law of equipartition of energy, what is the total internal energy of one mole of a rigid diatomic ideal gas at temperature T (translation and rotation only)?
questions.explanation: A rigid diatomic molecule has 5 degrees of freedom, each contributing ½RT per mole.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Helium (molar mass 4 g/mol) and oxygen (molar mass 32 g/mol) are at the same temperature. What is the ratio of the average translational kinetic energy per molecule of helium to that of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = (3/2)k_BT depends only on temperature, not on the type of gas.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Find the average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule at 27 °C. (Boltzmann constant = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Average translational KE per molecule is (3/2)k_BT = 6.21 × 10⁻²¹ J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: At the mean position of a particle executing SHM
questions.explanation: At the mean position displacement and acceleration are zero, speed and kinetic energy are maximum.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of angular frequency ω?
questions.explanation: ω = 2π/T, measured in radians per second.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle's displacement is x = 0.05 sin(20πt) metres. What is the frequency of oscillation?
questions.explanation: ω = 20π rad s⁻¹, so f = ω/2π = 10 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A mass–spring system is taken from the Earth to the Moon. Compared with the time period on Earth, the period on the Moon is
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k) does not depend on g, so it is unchanged.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle performs SHM of amplitude A and total energy E. What is its kinetic energy when the displacement is A/2?
questions.explanation: PE = E(x/A)² = E/4, so KE = E − E/4 = 3E/4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A mass m is attached to two identical springs, each of force constant k, connected in parallel. Compared with the time period for a single spring, the new period is
questions.explanation: Parallel springs have effective constant 2k, so T = 2π√(m/2k), which is 1/√2 of the single-spring period.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The length of a simple pendulum is decreased by 2%. By approximately what percentage does its time period change?
keyPoints: Fractional change in T = ½ × fractional change in l
questions.explanation: Because T depends on the square root of l, the percentage change is halved. A clock with such a pendulum would run fast.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In which type of medium is the speed of sound generally the largest?
questions.explanation: Solids are the most rigid, so sound travels fastest in them.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: When a source of sound moves towards a stationary listener, the apparent frequency heard by the listener
questions.explanation: This is the Doppler effect: an approaching source gives a higher apparent frequency.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A sound wave of frequency 170 Hz travels at 340 m s⁻¹. What is its wavelength?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A stationary wave on a string has wavelength 0.6 m. What is the distance between two consecutive nodes?
questions.explanation: Adjacent nodes are separated by λ/2 = 0.3 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The tension in a stretched string is made four times, with the mass per unit length unchanged. The speed of a transverse wave on the string becomes
questions.explanation: v = √(T/μ), so four times the tension doubles the speed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: An open organ pipe is 0.5 m long and the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. What is the fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: For an open pipe f = v/2L = 340/(2 × 0.5) = 340 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A string has mass per unit length 0.01 kg m⁻¹ and is under a tension of 4 N. Find the speed of a transverse wave on it.
questions.explanation: The wave speed on a stretched string is √(T/μ) = 20 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of cycles per unit time, so its dimensions are T⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many base quantities are there in the International System of Units (SI)?
questions.explanation: The seven SI base quantities are length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many significant figures are there in the number 0.00250 m?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant; the digits 2, 5 and the trailing 0 are, giving 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two lengths 2.675 m and 3.4 m are added. Which result is reported correctly with the proper number of significant decimal places?
questions.explanation: In addition the answer keeps as many decimal places as the least precise number (3.4 has one), so 6.075 is rounded to 6.1 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Planck's constant h is defined through E = hν, where E is energy and ν is frequency. What is its dimensional formula?
questions.explanation: h = E/ν = ML²T⁻² / T⁻¹ = ML²T⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The density of a solid cylinder is found from ρ = m/(πr²l). The mass m, radius r and length l are each measured with a 1% error. What is the maximum percentage error in the density?
questions.explanation: Error = 1% (mass) + 2 × 1% (radius squared) + 1% (length) = 4%.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Check by dimensions that the equation s = ut + ½at² is dimensionally correct.
questions.answer: Every term has the dimension of length, L, so the equation is dimensionally consistent.
questions.explanation: All terms on both sides have the same dimensions, L.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A student writes the kinetic energy of a body as KE = mv². Is the formula dimensionally correct? Does that prove that it is a correct physical formula?
questions.answer: Yes, it is dimensionally correct (ML²T⁻²), but dimensional correctness does not prove correctness: the actual formula is ½mv², because dimensional analysis cannot fix dimensionless constants such as ½.
keyPoints: Dimensional analysis cannot determine pure numbers like ½
Dimensional consistency is a necessary, not a sufficient, condition
questions.explanation: The correct expression is KE = ½mv²; the check only catches errors in dimensions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The magnitude of the instantaneous velocity of a particle is equal to its
questions.explanation: Instantaneous speed is the magnitude of the instantaneous velocity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A straight horizontal line in a velocity–time graph represents motion with
questions.explanation: A constant v means zero acceleration, i.e. uniform velocity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A body has initial velocity 5 m s⁻¹ and a uniform acceleration of 4 m s⁻². How far does it travel in 3 s?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A train moving at 30 m s⁻¹ is braked with a uniform deceleration of 5 m s⁻². How far does it travel before stopping?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A body starts from rest, accelerates uniformly to 8 m s⁻¹ in 4 s, and then moves at this constant speed for 6 s. What is the total distance covered in these 10 s?
questions.explanation: First 4 s: ½ × 4 × 8 = 16 m (area of triangle); next 6 s: 8 × 6 = 48 m; total 64 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Ball A is dropped from a high point. One second later ball B is dropped from the same point. While both are still falling, the distance between them
questions.explanation: Separation = ½g[t² − (t − 1)²] = ½g(2t − 1), which grows with t.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A car increases its speed uniformly from 10 m s⁻¹ to 30 m s⁻¹ in 10 s. Find its acceleration and the distance covered in this time.
questions.explanation: With uniform acceleration the distance equals average velocity times time.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 25 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find its height above the starting point at t = 1 s and at t = 4 s, and explain why the two heights are equal.
questions.answer: Height is 20 m at both t = 1 s and t = 4 s. At 1 s the ball is rising (velocity +15 m s⁻¹); at 4 s it is falling (velocity −15 m s⁻¹) through the same point.
keyPoints: Velocity at 1 s is +15 m s⁻¹; at 4 s is −15 m s⁻¹
The ball passes the same height twice, once going up and once coming down
questions.explanation: The ball reaches the top at 2.5 s, so t = 1 s and t = 4 s are symmetric about that instant.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The resultant of two equal vectors acting in exactly opposite directions is
questions.explanation: Equal magnitudes and opposite directions cancel, giving a null vector.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: At the highest point of its path, the velocity of a projectile is
questions.explanation: The vertical component vanishes at the top; the horizontal component remains unchanged.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the angular speed of the minute hand of a clock?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two perpendicular vectors have magnitudes 3 and 4. What is the magnitude of their vector (cross) product?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two forces of 10 N each act at a point with an angle of 120° between them. What is the magnitude of the resultant?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A projectile is fired at 45° to the horizontal. What is the relationship between its maximum height H and its horizontal range R?
questions.explanation: H = u² sin²45°/2g = u²/4g and R = u²/g, so H = R/4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A force of 6 N acts towards the east and a force of 8 N acts towards the north on the same body. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant.
questions.answer: 10 N, at about 53° north of east.
keyPoints: θ ≈ 53° from the east towards the north
questions.explanation: The forces are perpendicular, so Pythagoras gives the magnitude and tan⁻¹(8/6) the direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: An aeroplane flying horizontally at 100 m s⁻¹ at a height of 500 m releases a packet. Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and ignoring air resistance, find the time the packet takes to reach the ground and the horizontal distance it travels.
keyPoints: Vertical: 500 = ½ × 10 × t², so t = 10 s
questions.explanation: The packet keeps the plane's horizontal speed while falling freely.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The total linear momentum of a system is conserved when
options: no external force acts on it
no internal force acts on it
questions.explanation: From Newton's second law, if the net external force is zero the total momentum does not change.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Compared with sliding friction, rolling friction is generally
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction, which is why wheels are used.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the weight of a 5 kg body at a place where g = 9.8 m s⁻²?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 1 kg body on a smooth surface is acted on by two horizontal forces, 3 N and 4 N, in opposite directions. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Net force = 4 − 3 = 1 N, so a = 1/1 = 1 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 50 kg person stands on a weighing machine in a lift that is accelerating downward at 2 m s⁻². Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what force does the machine read?
questions.explanation: mg − N = ma, so N = m(g − a) = 50 × 8 = 400 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A block slides down a smooth incline of angle 30° with the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: a = g sinθ = 10 × 0.5 = 5 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Why do passengers in a bus lurch forward when the driver applies the brakes suddenly?
questions.answer: Because of inertia of motion: the passengers' bodies tend to continue moving forward at the original speed while the bus slows down.
keyPoints: Bus slows down due to braking
Passengers' bodies tend to retain their state of uniform motion (inertia)
So they move forward relative to the bus
questions.explanation: This is an everyday example of Newton's first law.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 2 kg block and a 3 kg block are joined by a light string on a smooth horizontal table. A horizontal force of 10 N pulls the 3 kg block away from the 2 kg block. Find the acceleration and the tension in the string.
keyPoints: The string alone accelerates the 2 kg block
questions.explanation: The tension is the only horizontal force on the 2 kg block, so T = ma = 4 N.
