questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A stretched spring possesses
questions.explanation: Work done in deforming the spring is stored as elastic potential energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 4 kg body has a kinetic energy of 50 J. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: ½ × 4 × v² = 50 gives v² = 25, so v = 5 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A constant force of 200 N moves a vehicle at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹ along the direction of the force. What is the power delivered?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A variable force F = 3x² newtons acts on a body, where x is in metres. How much work does it do in moving the body from x = 0 to x = 2 m?
questions.explanation: W = ∫₀² 3x² dx = [x³]₀² = 8 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A small car slides without friction down a track and into a vertical loop of radius r. From what minimum height above the lowest point of the loop must it be released from rest to just complete the loop?
questions.explanation: At the top, v² = gr, so energy conservation gives mgh = mg(2r) + ½m(gr), i.e. h = 2.5r.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A block is pushed 5 m along a floor against a constant friction force of 10 N. Find the work done by friction.
questions.explanation: Friction acts opposite to the displacement, so its work is negative.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 20 g bullet moving at 200 m s⁻¹ penetrates 10 cm into a wooden block and stops. Find the average resistive force exerted by the wood.
questions.explanation: The work done by the resistive force equals the bullet's initial kinetic energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The rotational analogue of mass in linear motion is
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia measures a body's resistance to change in its rotational motion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The torque of a force about an axis is zero when
options: its line of action passes through the axis
the force is perpendicular to the position vector
questions.explanation: τ = rF sinθ; if the line of action passes through the axis, the perpendicular distance is zero.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A wheel rotates at 120 revolutions per minute. What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: 120 rpm = 2 rev s⁻¹, so ω = 2 × 2π = 4π rad s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the moment of inertia of a uniform disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its plane?
questions.explanation: I = ½MR² = ½ × 2 × 0.25 = 0.25 kg m².

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A man stands on a freely rotating platform. Together they have a moment of inertia of 4 kg m² and rotate at 5 rad s⁻¹. The man stretches his arms so that the combined moment of inertia becomes 8 kg m². What is the new angular speed?
questions.explanation: L is conserved: 4 × 5 = 8 × ω, so ω = 2.5 rad s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A uniform light seesaw is balanced at its middle. A 40 kg child sits 1.5 m from the pivot. At what distance from the pivot on the other side must a 30 kg child sit to balance it?
questions.explanation: Balance of torques: 40 × 1.5 = 30 × d, so d = 2.0 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A flywheel starts from rest and has a constant angular acceleration of 2 rad s⁻². Find its angular speed and the angle turned after 10 s.
questions.answer: ω = 20 rad s⁻¹; angle turned = 100 rad.
questions.explanation: The equations of rotational kinematics mirror those of linear motion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Kepler's third law of planetary motion states that
questions.explanation: The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon's surface is about
questions.explanation: The Moon's surface gravity is roughly 1.6 m s⁻², about one-sixth of Earth's.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A planet has the same average density as the Earth but twice the Earth's radius. What is the acceleration due to gravity on its surface?
questions.explanation: g = (4/3)πGρR, so for the same density g is proportional to R, giving 2g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The Earth's escape speed is 11.2 km s⁻¹. What would be the escape speed from a planet of the same mass but half the radius?
questions.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/R) ∝ 1/√R, so halving R multiplies it by √2: 11.2 × 1.414 ≈ 15.8 km s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: For a communications satellite to appear fixed in the sky as seen from Earth, it must
options: orbit in a polar plane with a period of 24 hours
revolve in the equatorial plane, from west to east, with a period of 24 hours
revolve in the equatorial plane, from east to west, with a period of 12 hours
revolve at a height of about 400 km
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite must match the Earth's rotation: same period, same direction and an equatorial orbit.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: An astronaut inside a satellite orbiting the Earth feels weightless because
options: gravity is zero at that height
the Moon cancels the Earth's attraction
both the astronaut and the satellite are in free fall with the same acceleration
questions.explanation: Gravity still acts, but the astronaut and the satellite fall together, so there is no normal force between them.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², the radius of the Earth R = 6.4 × 10⁶ m and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², estimate the mass of the Earth.
questions.explanation: gR² = 4.01 × 10¹⁴; dividing by G gives about 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Strain is
questions.explanation: Strain is a ratio of two lengths (or volumes), so it has no dimensions or unit.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Elasticity is the property of a body by which it
options: breaks when a force is applied
regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed
questions.explanation: This is the definition of elasticity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A shear stress of 10⁵ Pa produces a shear strain of 10⁻⁶. What is the shear modulus of the material?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus = shear stress/shear strain = 10⁵/10⁻⁶ = 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire of length 1 m and cross-section 1 mm² extends by 0.25 mm under a load of 50 N. What is its Young's modulus?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire of cross-sectional area 2 mm² has a breaking stress of 5 × 10⁸ N m⁻². What is the maximum load it can carry without breaking?
questions.explanation: F = stress × area = 5 × 10⁸ × 2 × 10⁻⁶ = 1000 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Stress–strain graphs for the elastic region of two wires of the same dimensions are straight lines through the origin. Wire 1's line is steeper than wire 2's. Which statement is correct?
options: Wire 1 has the larger Young's modulus
Wire 2 has the larger Young's modulus
questions.explanation: The slope of a stress–strain graph is Young's modulus, so the steeper line indicates the larger modulus.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A steel wire and a copper wire have the same length and cross-sectional area and carry the same load. Young's modulus is 2 × 10¹¹ Pa for steel and 1.1 × 10¹¹ Pa for copper. Which stretches more, and by what ratio?
questions.answer: The copper wire stretches more, about 1.8 times as much as the steel wire.
questions.explanation: With F, L and A equal, the wire with the smaller Young's modulus extends more.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is about

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: When the temperature of a liquid is increased, its coefficient of viscosity generally
questions.explanation: In liquids, viscosity falls as temperature rises (in gases it rises).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Water flows in a pipe of cross-section 4 cm² at 3 m s⁻¹ and then enters a narrower section of cross-section 2 cm². What is its speed in the narrower section?
questions.explanation: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ gives v₂ = 4 × 3 / 2 = 6 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A force of 200 N acts uniformly and perpendicularly on a surface of area 0.5 m². What is the pressure?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Ice has a density of 900 kg m⁻³ and floats in fresh water of density 1000 kg m⁻³. What percentage of the ice's volume is above the water surface?
questions.explanation: The submerged fraction is 900/1000 = 90%, so 10% is above the surface.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A spherical water drop of radius R splits into 8 identical small droplets. How does the total surface area change?
questions.explanation: Each droplet has radius R/2, so the total area is 8 × 4π(R/2)² = 2 × 4πR².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Find the absolute pressure at a depth of 20 m in a lake. Take atmospheric pressure = 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³ and g = 10 m s⁻².
questions.explanation: Absolute pressure is atmospheric pressure plus the gauge pressure ρgh.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A metal block of volume 0.001 m³ and density 8000 kg m⁻³ is held fully immersed in water (density 1000 kg m⁻³). Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find its apparent weight in water.
questions.explanation: Apparent weight equals true weight minus the buoyant force.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of the coefficient of linear expansion?
questions.explanation: α = ΔL/(L ΔT), so its unit is per kelvin.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Water has its maximum density at
questions.explanation: Water is densest at about 4 °C, an anomalous behaviour of water.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A heat input of 500 J raises the temperature of a 0.1 kg object by 5 K. What is the specific heat capacity of the material?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A solid has a coefficient of linear expansion of 1 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. What is its coefficient of volume expansion?
questions.explanation: For a solid, γ = 3α = 3 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: As the temperature of a hot body is raised, the wavelength at which it emits the maximum radiation
questions.explanation: Wien's displacement law: λ_max T = constant, so higher T gives smaller λ_max.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How much heat is needed to convert 10 g of ice at 0 °C into water at 20 °C? (L = 80 cal g⁻¹, c of water = 1 cal g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Melting needs 10 × 80 = 800 cal; warming the water by 20 °C needs 10 × 1 × 20 = 200 cal; total 1000 cal.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 200 g piece of metal at 100 °C is dropped into 100 g of water at 20 °C. The final temperature is 30 °C. The specific heat of water is 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹. Find the specific heat of the metal (ignore heat losses).
keyPoints: Heat lost by metal = heat gained by water
questions.explanation: Using the principle of calorimetry, the heat lost by the hot metal equals the heat gained by the water.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Heat flows spontaneously
options: from a cold body to a hot body
from a hot body to a cold body
only from the sink to the source
questions.explanation: Experience, expressed by the second law, shows heat flows from higher to lower temperature on its own.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In an adiabatic process
options: no heat is exchanged with the surroundings
questions.explanation: Adiabatic means Q = 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: 300 J of work is done on a gas and the gas loses 100 J of heat to the surroundings. What is the change in its internal energy?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A Carnot engine whose sink is at 300 K has an efficiency of 40%. What is the temperature of its source?
questions.explanation: η = 1 − T₂/T₁ gives T₂/T₁ = 0.6, so T₁ = 300/0.6 = 500 K.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A gas is taken around a rectangular cycle on a P–V diagram. Pressure varies between 1 × 10⁵ Pa and 3 × 10⁵ Pa and volume between 1 litre and 2 litres (1 litre = 10⁻³ m³). What net work is done in one cycle?
questions.explanation: Net work = area of the rectangle = (2 × 10⁵ Pa)(10⁻³ m³) = 200 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 1 mol of a monatomic ideal gas by 10 K at constant pressure? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: For a monatomic gas Cp = (5/2)R, so Q = 2.5 × 8.31 × 10 ≈ 208 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Find the change in internal energy of 1 mol of a monatomic ideal gas when its temperature rises by 20 K. (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Internal energy change of an ideal gas depends only on ΔT: ΔU = nCvΔT.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Real gases behave most nearly like an ideal gas at
questions.explanation: At low pressure the molecules are far apart and at high temperature intermolecular forces matter less.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to the kinetic theory, the pressure exerted by a gas is due to
options: collisions of the molecules with the walls of the container
questions.explanation: Molecules striking the walls transfer momentum, producing a steady average force per unit area.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many moles are there in 88 g of carbon dioxide (molar mass 44 g mol⁻¹)?
questions.explanation: n = mass/molar mass = 88/44 = 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A gas in a rigid container is at a pressure of 2 atm at 300 K. What is the pressure when it is heated to 450 K?
questions.explanation: At constant volume P/T is constant: P = 2 × 450/300 = 3 atm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The mean free path of a gas molecule is inversely proportional to the number of molecules per unit volume. If the number density is doubled (same molecular size), the mean free path
questions.explanation: λ = 1/(√2 π d² n), so doubling n halves λ.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the ratio of specific heats γ = Cp/Cv for a rigid diatomic ideal gas?
questions.explanation: With 5 degrees of freedom, Cv = (5/2)R and Cp = (7/2)R, so γ = 7/5 = 1.4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Calculate the rms speed of nitrogen molecules at 300 K. (Molar mass of N₂ = 28 g mol⁻¹, R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: 3 × 8.31 × 300 = 7479; dividing by 0.028 gives 2.67 × 10⁵, whose square root is about 517.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The maximum displacement of an oscillating particle from its mean position is called its
questions.explanation: That is the definition of amplitude.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In SHM, the phase difference between the displacement and the velocity of the particle is
questions.explanation: If x = A sin ωt, then v = Aω cos ωt, which differs in phase by π/2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Roughly what is the length of a 'seconds pendulum' (time period 2 s) at a place where g = 9.8 m s⁻²?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle's displacement is x = 3 sin(2t) metres, with t in seconds. What is its displacement at t = π/4 s?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A pendulum clock keeps correct time at sea level. It is taken to the top of a high mountain where g is slightly smaller. The clock will
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g) increases when g decreases, so each tick takes longer and the clock loses time.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A mass hung from a vertical spring stretches it by 10 cm at equilibrium. If the mass is pulled down slightly and released, what is the time period of its oscillation? (Take g = 10 m s⁻².)
questions.explanation: At equilibrium mg = kx, so m/k = x/g; T = 2π√(x/g) = 2π√(0.1/10) = 0.63 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle performs SHM with amplitude 2 cm and frequency 5 Hz. Find its maximum acceleration. (Use π² = 9.87.)
questions.explanation: Maximum acceleration is ω²A = 987 × 0.02 ≈ 19.7 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a transverse wave?
options: A wave on a stretched string
questions.explanation: On a stretched string the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of travel.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to the principle of superposition, when two waves overlap at a point, the resultant displacement is
options: the algebraic sum of the individual displacements
the difference of the amplitudes only
the larger of the two displacements
questions.explanation: The net displacement is the algebraic (vector) sum of the displacements due to each wave.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A person shouts towards a cliff and hears the echo 2 s later. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, how far away is the cliff?
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back in 2 s, so the distance is 340 × 2 / 2 = 340 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A pipe closed at one end is 0.25 m long. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, what is its fundamental frequency?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In a pipe closed at one end, the frequency of the first overtone is how many times the fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: A closed pipe supports only odd harmonics (f, 3f, 5f, …), so the first overtone is 3f.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A train sounding a horn of frequency 500 Hz approaches a stationary listener at 34 m s⁻¹. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, what frequency does the listener hear?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Distinguish between transverse and longitudinal waves, giving one example of each.
questions.answer: In a transverse wave the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of propagation (example: waves on a string); in a longitudinal wave they vibrate parallel to it (example: sound in air).
keyPoints: Transverse: particle motion perpendicular to wave direction; crests and troughs
Longitudinal: particle motion parallel to wave direction; compressions and rarefactions
questions.explanation: The distinction lies in the direction of particle vibration relative to the direction of wave travel.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: The ampere is the SI base unit of electric current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity = length/time = LT⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of linear momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity = M × LT⁻¹ = MLT⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A screw gauge has a pitch of 1 mm and 100 divisions on its circular scale. What is its least count?
questions.explanation: Least count = pitch / number of circular divisions = 1/100 = 0.01 mm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities can be added to a quantity with dimensions ML²T⁻²?
questions.explanation: Only quantities with the same dimensions can be added; torque has dimensions ML²T⁻², like energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In a pendulum experiment g = 4π²l/T². The length is l = 100.0 cm with an error of 0.1 cm, and the period is T = 2.00 s with an error of 0.02 s. What is the percentage error in g?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Express a speed of 54 km/h in m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Multiplying km/h by 5/18 gives m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Stokes' law gives the viscous force on a sphere as F = 6πηrv. Use this to find the dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity η.
questions.explanation: The numerical factor 6π is dimensionless, so only F, r and v matter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A runner completes one full lap of a circular track and returns to the starting point. His displacement is
questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line change in position, which is zero when he ends where he began.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The slope of a velocity–time graph gives
questions.explanation: Slope of v–t graph = dv/dt = acceleration.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A car starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 3 m s⁻². What is its speed after 6 s?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: An object is dropped from rest. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², how far does it fall in 2 s?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 20 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). What is its average speed over the first 4 s of motion?
questions.explanation: It rises 20 m in 2 s and falls 20 m in the next 2 s, so the distance is 40 m and the average speed is 40/4 = 10 m s⁻¹ (average velocity is zero).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two cars 500 m apart approach each other along a straight road at constant speeds of 20 m s⁻¹ and 30 m s⁻¹. After how long do they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 50 m s⁻¹, so time = 500/50 = 10 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A stone is dropped from a height of 80 m (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find the time it takes to reach the ground and its speed on impact.
questions.explanation: Free fall from rest: h = ½gt² and v = gt.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A driver travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ sees an obstacle and applies the brakes after a reaction time of 0.5 s. The car then decelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻². Find the total distance travelled from the moment the obstacle is seen until the car stops.
questions.explanation: The car moves at constant speed during the reaction time and then decelerates uniformly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration of the body is directed
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration points along the radius towards the centre.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The scalar product of two perpendicular vectors is
questions.explanation: A · B = AB cos 90° = 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the horizontal component of a velocity of 20 m s⁻¹ directed 60° above the horizontal?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle moves on a circle of radius 2 m with a speed of 4π m s⁻¹. What is its time period?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 60° to the horizontal. What is its speed at the highest point of its path?
questions.explanation: Only the horizontal component remains at the top: 20 cos 60° = 10 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Rain falls vertically at 10 m s⁻¹. A man walks on a level road at 10 m s⁻¹. At what angle to the vertical should he tilt his umbrella to keep dry?
options: 45°, tilted forward (in the direction he walks)
questions.explanation: Relative to the man the rain has a horizontal component of 10 m s⁻¹ towards him and a vertical one of 10 m s⁻¹, so it comes from 45° ahead of him.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Find the horizontal range of a projectile launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 45° (g = 10 m s⁻², level ground).
questions.explanation: At 45° the range is u²/g = 40 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is struck at 30 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal (g = 10 m s⁻², level ground, no air resistance). Find the maximum height and the horizontal range.
questions.explanation: Apply the standard formulae with sin 30° = 0.5 and sin 60° = 0.866.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: One newton is equal to
questions.explanation: F = ma, so 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The force of friction between two surfaces acts
options: opposite to the relative motion (or its tendency)
questions.explanation: Friction opposes the relative motion, or the tendency of relative motion, between the surfaces.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the momentum of a 2 kg body moving at 5 m s⁻¹?
questions.explanation: p = mv = 2 × 5 = 10 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 5 kg block rests on a table. A string attached to it pulls it vertically upward with a force of 20 N (the block stays on the table). Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the normal force from the table?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 4 kg block on a smooth horizontal table is connected by a light string over a smooth pulley at the table edge to a 1 kg block hanging freely. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the acceleration of the system?
questions.explanation: a = m₂g/(m₁ + m₂) = 10/5 = 2 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A frictionless road is banked so that a car can negotiate a bend of radius 40 m at 20 m s⁻¹ without any friction. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the angle of banking?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 2000 kg truck is acted on by a net force of 5000 N. Find its acceleration and the speed it reaches from rest after 4 s.
questions.answer: Acceleration = 2.5 m s⁻²; speed after 4 s = 10 m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Use Newton's second law and then v = u + at with u = 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 2 kg block rests on top of a 4 kg block that lies on a smooth floor. The coefficient of friction between the blocks is 0.3. What is the maximum horizontal force that can be applied to the lower block so that the upper block does not slip? (g = 10 m s⁻².)
keyPoints: Maximum acceleration of the upper block = μg = 3 m s⁻²
Both blocks must share this acceleration
questions.explanation: Friction on the upper block can supply at most μmg, limiting the common acceleration to μg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The work done by a force is zero when the force is
questions.explanation: W = Fs cosθ is zero when θ = 90°.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: One joule is the same as one
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance, so 1 J = 1 N m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: KE ∝ v², so doubling v multiplies KE by 4.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: Work = mgh = 6000 J; power = 6000/20 = 300 W.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: It falls 1 m, so v = √(2gl) = √20 ≈ 4.5 m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball dropped from a height of 4 m rebounds to a height of 1 m. Find the coefficient of restitution.
questions.explanation: e is the ratio of the speed after to the speed before the collision.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A train engine delivers a constant power of 20 kW while the train moves at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹. Find the resistive force acting on the train.
keyPoints: At constant speed, driving force = resistive force
questions.explanation: With zero acceleration the driving force equals the resistance, and P = Fv.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the SI unit of the moment of inertia?
questions.explanation: I = Σmr², so its unit is kg m².

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The angular momentum of a system is conserved when

the net external torque is zero
questions.explanation: Since τ = dL/dt, L is constant when the net external torque vanishes.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A wheel of radius 0.5 m rotates at 10 rad s⁻¹. What is the linear speed of a point on its rim?

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A solid disc rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface. What fraction of its total kinetic energy is rotational?
questions.explanation: Rotational KE = ½ × ½MR² × (v/R)² = Mv²/4; total = 3Mv²/4; the fraction is 1/3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A uniform horizontal beam of mass 10 kg and length 4 m is hinged at one end and supported at the other end. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what force does the support exert?
questions.explanation: Taking torques about the hinge: F × 4 = 100 × 2, so F = 50 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A particle of mass 2 kg moves in a circle of radius 0.5 m at a speed of 4 m s⁻¹. Find its angular momentum about the centre.
keyPoints: L = m v r (velocity is perpendicular to radius)
questions.explanation: For circular motion, L = mvr.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The value of the acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface is approximately
questions.explanation: Near the Earth's surface g ≈ 9.8 m s⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The universal law of gravitation was proposed by
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton stated that every particle attracts every other with a force proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r², so doubling r divides F by 4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to twice the Earth's radius above the surface?
questions.explanation: The distance from the centre is 3R, so g' = g R²/(3R)² = g/9.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: For a satellite in a circular orbit, what is the ratio of its kinetic energy to the magnitude of its gravitational potential energy?
questions.explanation: KE = GMm/2r and |PE| = GMm/r, so the ratio is 1/2.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is 1.6 m s⁻². What would a 60 kg person weigh on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Mass is the same everywhere; only the weight changes with local g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Hooke's law holds good within the
questions.explanation: Stress is proportional to strain only within the elastic limit.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain is called
questions.explanation: This ratio is Young's modulus.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A force of 100 N is applied uniformly over a cross-section of 2 cm². What is the stress?
questions.explanation: Stress = 100/(2 × 10⁻⁴ m²) = 5 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire is subjected to a stress of 4 × 10⁸ Pa and shows a strain of 0.002. What is its Young's modulus?
questions.explanation: Y = stress/strain = 4 × 10⁸/0.002 = 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire of length 2 m, cross-section 1 mm² and Young's modulus 2 × 10¹¹ Pa behaves like a spring. What is its force constant k = YA/L?

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wire of force constant k is cut into two equal halves. What is the force constant of each half?
questions.explanation: k = YA/L, so halving L doubles k.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Why are steel cables, rather than rubber ropes, used in cranes to lift heavy loads?
questions.answer: Steel has a much larger Young's modulus than rubber, so it stretches very little under a heavy load and stays within its elastic limit.
keyPoints: Steel has a high Young's modulus
Small strain for a given stress
Remains within elastic limit and is strong
questions.explanation: A larger Young's modulus means less extension for the same stress.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Bernoulli's principle is based on the conservation of
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's equation is an expression of energy conservation for a flowing ideal fluid.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: In streamline (steady) flow of a fluid
options: the velocity at any given point remains constant with time
the velocity changes irregularly at every point
the fluid rotates about every point
questions.explanation: In steady flow every fluid particle passing a given point has the same velocity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A wooden block of volume 2 × 10⁻³ m³ is held completely under water (density 1000 kg m⁻³). Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the buoyant force?
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = ρVg = 1000 × 2 × 10⁻³ × 10 = 20 N.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: Flow rate ∝ r⁴, so 2⁴ = 16 times.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The height to which a liquid rises in a capillary tube is inversely proportional to the radius of the tube. If a tube of half the radius is used, the height of the rise
questions.explanation: h = 2S cosθ/(rρg) ∝ 1/r, so halving r doubles h.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Why do small drops of mercury on a smooth surface take an almost spherical shape?
questions.answer: Because of surface tension: a liquid surface tends to have the least possible area, and a sphere has the smallest surface area for a given volume.
keyPoints: Surface tension tends to minimise surface area
A sphere has minimum surface area for a given volume
Gravity is negligible for very small drops
questions.explanation: Minimising surface energy leads to a spherical shape.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Water flows steadily through a pipe of radius 2 cm at a speed of 1 m s⁻¹. The pipe narrows to a radius of 1 cm. Find the speed in the narrow section and the volume flow rate.
questions.answer: Speed = 4 m s⁻¹; volume flow rate ≈ 1.26 × 10⁻³ m³ s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: The flow rate Av is the same in every section.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: c = Q/(mΔT), with unit J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: An ideal black body is one that
options: reflects all radiation falling on it
transmits all radiation falling on it
absorbs none of the radiation falling on it
absorbs all radiation falling on it
questions.explanation: A perfect black body absorbs all incident radiation (and is also the best emitter).

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How much heat is needed to melt 2 kg of ice at 0 °C? (L = 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.)

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A bimetallic strip made of two metals with different coefficients of linear expansion is heated. What happens?
options: It bends, with the metal of larger expansion coefficient on the outer (convex) side
It bends, with the metal of larger expansion coefficient on the inner (concave) side
It expands only along its length
questions.explanation: The metal that expands more becomes longer, so it lies on the outside of the curve.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two rods of equal length and cross-section are joined end to end. Rod A has thermal conductivity 2k and rod B has k. The free end of A is held at 100 °C and the free end of B at 0 °C. What is the steady-state temperature at the junction?
questions.explanation: Equal heat flow: 2k(100 − T) = k(T − 0), so 200 = 3T and T = 66.7 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A 1 kW heater is used to heat 0.5 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C. Taking c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ignoring losses, find the time required.
questions.explanation: Energy supplied by the heater equals the heat absorbed by the water.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A process that takes place at constant pressure is called
questions.explanation: 'Isobaric' means constant pressure.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: An ideal gas has no intermolecular potential energy, so U depends only on T.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A gas is compressed at a constant pressure of 1 × 10⁵ Pa from 3 litres to 1 litre (1 litre = 10⁻³ m³). What is the work involved?
questions.explanation: |W| = PΔV = 10⁵ × 2 × 10⁻³ = 200 J; since the volume decreases, the work is done on the gas.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A diatomic ideal gas (γ = 1.4) is compressed adiabatically to half its volume. By what factor does its pressure increase? (Use 2^1.4 ≈ 2.64.)
questions.explanation: PV^γ is constant, so P₂/P₁ = (V₁/V₂)^γ = 2^1.4 ≈ 2.64.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A heat engine of efficiency 30% does 600 J of work per cycle. How much heat does it reject to the sink per cycle?
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed = 600/0.3 = 2000 J; heat rejected = 2000 − 600 = 1400 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: State the first law of thermodynamics and write its mathematical form.
questions.answer: The heat supplied to a system equals the increase in its internal energy plus the work done by the system: Q = ΔU + W.
keyPoints: It is a statement of energy conservation
Q = heat supplied, ΔU = change in internal energy, W = work done by the system
questions.explanation: Heat supplied is shared between raising internal energy and doing work.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to classical kinetic theory, the kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas at absolute zero is
questions.explanation: KE ∝ T, so it would vanish at T = 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The value of the universal gas constant R is about
questions.explanation: R ≈ 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (while 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ is the Boltzmann constant).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many molecules are there in 2 g of hydrogen gas (H₂, molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹)?
questions.explanation: 2 g of H₂ is one mole, which contains 6.022 × 10²³ molecules.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: At constant temperature the volume of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is halved. Its pressure
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law PV is constant, so halving V doubles P.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A container holds 2 mol of gas A and 3 mol of gas B at a total pressure of 5 atm (ideal gases, no reaction). What is the partial pressure of A?
questions.explanation: Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure = (2/5) × 5 = 2 atm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the ratio of the rms speed of the molecules of a gas at 400 K to that at 100 K?
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ √T, so the ratio is √(400/100) = 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many molecules are there in 1 litre of an ideal gas at STP? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 L, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Divide Avogadro's number by the molar volume in litres.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g) depends on l and g only.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Why does the amplitude of a real oscillating pendulum gradually decrease with time?
questions.answer: Because of damping: air resistance and friction at the support dissipate the pendulum's mechanical energy as heat.
keyPoints: Mechanical energy is gradually lost as heat
questions.explanation: The energy of an oscillator is proportional to the square of its amplitude, so energy loss reduces the amplitude.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (1 Hz = 1 s⁻¹).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The audible range of frequencies for a normal human ear is approximately
questions.explanation: Humans typically hear from about 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Two waves of amplitudes 3 units and 1 unit superpose to produce beats. What is the ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity?
questions.explanation: Maximum amplitude = 4, minimum = 2; intensity ∝ amplitude², so the ratio is 16 : 4 = 4 : 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A string 0.6 m long is fixed at both ends and the wave speed on it is 120 m s⁻¹. What is the frequency of its third harmonic?
questions.explanation: Fundamental f₁ = v/2L = 120/1.2 = 100 Hz; the third harmonic is 3 × 100 = 300 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ship's sonar sends an ultrasonic pulse down and receives the echo from the sea bed 0.2 s later. If the speed of sound in sea water is 1500 m s⁻¹, find the depth of the water.
questions.explanation: The pulse travels to the sea bed and back, so the depth is half the total path.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the unit of force in the CGS system?
questions.explanation: The dyne is the CGS unit of force (g cm s⁻²).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many dynes are there in one newton?
questions.explanation: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻² = 1000 g × 100 cm s⁻² = 10⁵ dyne.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: How many significant figures does the number 100.50 have?
questions.explanation: Zeros between non-zero digits and trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant, so all 5 digits count.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: Average velocity = displacement divided by the time taken.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity near the Earth's surface is directed
options: downward, towards the centre of the Earth
in the direction of the object's motion
questions.explanation: Gravity always pulls towards the centre of the Earth, whatever the direction of motion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 15 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its velocity after 1 s?
questions.explanation: v = u − gt = 15 − 10 = 5 m s⁻¹, still upward.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A body starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s⁻². How far does it travel during the 3rd second alone?
questions.explanation: Distance in 3 s = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 m; in 2 s = 4 m; so the 3rd second covers 5 m.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: A · B = AB cosθ is a number with no direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: The vector product A × B is directed
options: perpendicular to the plane containing A and B
questions.explanation: By the right-hand rule, A × B is perpendicular to both A and B.

questions.explanation: The net force equals the rate of change of momentum.

questions.explanation: Limiting static friction is slightly larger than kinetic friction, and rolling friction is far smaller.

questions.explanation: At rest, T = mg = 10 × 10 = 100 N.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: KE = loss of PE = mgh = 3 × 10 × 5 = 150 J.

questions.q: A 0.1 kg ball hits a wall perpendicularly at 10 m s⁻¹ and bounces back elastically with the same speed. What is the magnitude of the change in its momentum?

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: Angular velocity is the angle turned per unit time, in rad s⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics

its large moment of inertia resists sudden changes in rotational speed
questions.explanation: The large moment of inertia keeps the rotation smooth by opposing speed fluctuations.

questions.explanation: I_ring = MR² and I_disc = ½MR², giving a ratio 2 : 1.

questions.subject: physics

questions.q: A uniform metre stick is balanced on a knife edge at the 50 cm mark. A 100 g mass hangs at the 20 cm mark. What mass must hang at the 80 cm mark to keep it balanced?
questions.explanation: Both masses are 30 cm from the pivot, so their torques balance only if the masses are equal.

questions.subject: physics

questions.answer: I = 0.18 kg m²; torque = 0.9 N m.
questions.explanation: For a ring all the mass is at distance R from the axis.

questions.subject: physics

options: the mass of the planet and the orbital radius
questions.explanation: v = √(GM/r) depends on the planet's mass M and the orbital radius r, not on the satellite's mass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: According to Kepler's first law, the orbit of a planet is
options: a circle with the Sun at the centre
an ellipse with the Sun at the centre
an ellipse with the Sun at one focus
questions.explanation: Planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one of the foci.

questions.subject: physics

questions.explanation: Internal energy depends only on the state of the system; heat and work depend on the process.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: Which of the following is forbidden by the second law of thermodynamics?
options: Heat flowing from a hot body to a cold body
A cyclic engine converting all the heat from a single reservoir into work
Work being converted completely into heat
A gas expanding into a vacuum
questions.explanation: The Kelvin–Planck statement rules out a cyclic engine with 100% conversion of heat to work.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: An ideal gas is compressed isothermally. What happens to the heat?
options: The gas gives out heat equal to the work done on it
The gas absorbs heat from the surroundings
The internal energy of the gas increases
questions.explanation: ΔU = 0 for an isothermal process, so Q = W; since W is negative (work done on the gas), Q is negative: heat is released.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: 2 mol of an ideal gas with Cv = 12.5 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ is heated at constant volume through 10 K. How much heat is absorbed?
questions.explanation: Q = nCvΔT = 2 × 12.5 × 10 = 250 J (no work is done at constant volume).

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A refrigerator has a coefficient of performance of 5. How much work is needed to remove 1000 J of heat from the cold space?
questions.explanation: COP = Q_cold/W, so W = 1000/5 = 200 J.

questions.explanation: For an adiabatic process PV^γ = constant with γ > 1, so the curve falls more steeply than an isotherm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A gas absorbs 400 J of heat and does 150 J of work. Find the change in its internal energy.
questions.explanation: The heat not converted into work raises the internal energy.

questions.explanation: k_B = R/N_A ≈ 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: What is the density of oxygen gas (molar mass 32 g mol⁻¹) at STP? (Molar volume = 22.4 L.)
questions.explanation: Density = 32 g / 22.4 L ≈ 1.43 g L⁻¹ = 1.43 kg m⁻³.

questions.explanation: Average KE = (3/2)k_BT is proportional to T, so it doubles.

questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ 1/√M, so the ratio is √(2/4) = 1/√2.

questions.q: How many moles of a gas are there in 3.011 × 10²³ molecules? (N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Divide the number of molecules by Avogadro's number.

questions.q: A mass on a spring of force constant 40π² N m⁻¹ has a time period of 1 s. What is the mass?
questions.explanation: T² = 4π²m/k, so m = kT²/(4π²) = 40π²/(4π²) = 10 kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle in SHM has displacement x = A cos ωt. At t = 0 which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: At t = 0 the particle is at the extreme position x = A, where speed and KE are zero and PE is maximum.

questions.subject: physics
questions.q: A particle performs SHM with a time period of 4 s and amplitude 8 cm, starting from the mean position. How long does it take to reach a displacement of 4 cm?
questions.explanation: x = A sin ωt gives sin ωt = 0.5, so ωt = π/6 and t = T/12 = 1/3 s.

questions.explanation: The effective gravity becomes g + a, which is larger, so T = 2π√(l/g_eff) decreases.

questions.q: A 2 kg mass attached to a spring oscillates with a time period of 0.628 s. Find the force constant of the spring.
questions.explanation: Rearranging T = 2π√(m/k) gives k = 4π²m/T².

questions.explanation: Ultrasound lies above the audible range, i.e. above about 20 kHz.

questions.q: A wave is given by y = 0.1 sin(4πt − 2πx) in SI units. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: ω = 4π rad s⁻¹, so f = ω/2π = 2 Hz.
